meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: Well, I thought I'd start just by understanding a bit about sort of your current situation and situation with the property as well at the interest in short lane. Then we can go through some figures in our service if it sort of lines on what you're looking for.

meeting_flow.close_phrase: What we could do is we can keep in touch. Obviously keep in touch once a month or so... I'll just send a bit of a summary of everything we've spoken about, like an action plan, and then I'll also send our management agreement as well.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I'd rather have it be a combination [of guest types]... it leaves me in the lurch when something big happens in the country.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: That's exactly right... we don't cater exclusively to business professionals; we work on a mixed guest area, and the income estimates already reflect how we'd operate it anyway.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: And then also with the Leisure side is affected... I would want to know that I'm covered if something else big happens here.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I'd be surprised if it reaches that, but maybe I'm wrong (reacting to the higher end of the income range, ~£2,500/month net)
lead_responses.category: skepticism about income projection upper bound
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Explained the figures are comparable-based, that the area's low review density means a ramp-up period is likely, cited ~10% accuracy either side, and a roughly 4-month period before figures approach the projection
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Yeah (moved on, later said the overall figures were healthier than expected)

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Once before I had a business couple staying... the contractor said the washing machine wasn't working because I hadn't loaded it enough... if I ended up paying hundreds of pounds for things like that frequently, it wouldn't be worth my while. It's difficult with one beds because they don't earn so much.
lead_responses.category: maintenance cost anxiety / prior bad contractor experience
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Explained the tiered priority system, a £300/month pre-approval threshold with sign-off required above it, that a detailed onboarding form reduces recurring appliance issues over time, and framed maintenance as normally under 5% of gross while acknowledging that hits harder on a one-bed
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Because I take out insurance on my white goods... they tend to be two, three days before they come out, or maybe even a week. So could I still do that?

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Do you only offer full management or do you offer partial as well?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: No, we only offer full management, because if I'm not fully in control of the property, it's very hard for me to deliver a good service.

what_they_focused_on: Guaranteeing a mixed guest profile so income doesn't depend on a single segment again
Concrete maintenance cost controls and thresholds given a past overcharging experience
Whether her existing white-goods insurance response time would be workable
Whether full management was the only option (no partial)
what_they_needed_most: Explicit process detail and safeguards (tiered maintenance, spend thresholds) rather than general reassurance
Acknowledgement that a one-bed's fixed costs and fees bite harder against lower gross revenue
Confirmation the figures had genuinely improved since her pre-Covid experience
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For returning STL-SW leads on a single low-bedroom property, proactively frame the maintenance buffer and fee impact relative to gross revenue (not just the generic 5% line) before they have to raise it themselves, and lead with the mixed-guest-profile point early given her Covid-driven single-segment scare
